processing_steps.method: near-rapid solidification in a centrifugal casting equipment (melt poured into a rotating copper mold)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingot made from high purity Fe/Mn/Al/C/Cr, reheated to melt by an induction coil and poured into a copper mold at a rotating speed of 600 r/min under Ar atmosphere; obtained strip size (60–80) mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm. The 3Cr strip was produced by this near-rapid solidification route.
Annealed at 550 °C for 1 h in a vacuum electric resistance furnace. This 1 h anneal is one of the 550 °C annealing-time series (1, 5, 9 h) that was applied only to the 3Cr strip (Fig. 11).

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase austenite (γ) + ferrite (δ) structure, austenite being the major matrix phase with dispersed δ-ferrite; after annealing at 550 °C for 1 h the austenite matrix contains a dense tangled dislocation network and nano-scale κ-carbides precipitated during the first hour of annealing.

phases_present.morphology: nano-scale precipitates; in 3Cr too small to identify (superlattice very weak)

precipitates.distribution: nano-scale precipitates in the austenite matrix; mainly precipitated in the first hour of annealing treatment

microstructure_list.region: δ-ferrite particles dispersed in the austenite matrix

phases_present.volume_fraction: 11.4 vol% (as-cast value; ferrite size and fraction in annealed strips almost remain the same)
phases_present.morphology: particles dispersed in the austenite matrix

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: 3Cr strip annealed at 550 °C for 1 h; engineering stress–strain curve of the "550°C1h" specimen in Fig. 11(a)

ultimate_tensile_strength.value: slightly above 800 MPa (plateau level read from Fig. 11(a))

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve of the 550 °C/1 h 3Cr specimen rises steeply from the origin to a plateau slightly above the 800 MPa gridline; it stops at clearly lower strain than the 550 °C/9 h curve, which extends to ~50% strain (Fig. 11(a)).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEM-2100F, operated at a voltage of 200 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: BF imaging of the 1 h annealed 3Cr specimen; 500 nm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the dislocation structure in the austenite of the 3Cr strip annealed at 550 °C for 1 h (Fig. 11(b)).
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 1 h specimen shows individual dislocation lines in a dense, tangled arrangement (three dislocations arrowed).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: MTS Criterion Model 44 mechanical property tester with a 10 kN capacity
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: strain rate 1 × 10^-3 s^-1; gauge size 20 mm × 4 mm × 1 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the mechanical properties of the 3Cr strip annealed at 550 °C for different times, including 1 h (Fig. 11(a)).
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 1 h annealed curve plateaus slightly above 800 MPa and terminates at clearly lower strain than the 9 h curve; plasticity of the 3Cr strip increases with annealing time while the yield strength does not change significantly after 1 h annealing.

characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the actual composition of the strips (Table 1).
characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured composition of the 3Cr strip: Mn 27.6, Al 8.4, C 1.3, Cr 2.8 wt.%, Fe balance.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SJ-600G Electronic Water Displacement Density Analyzer
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the average density of the strips.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The measured average density of the 3Cr strip is 6.45 g/cm3.

unmapped_findings: The 550 °C annealing-time series (1, 5, 9 h) was studied only for the 3Cr strip (Fig. 11); the yield strength does not change significantly after 1 h annealing, while the plasticity of the 3Cr strip increases gradually with increasing annealing time.

For the 3Cr strip annealed at 550 °C, the dislocation density gradually decreases with increasing annealing time (Fig. 11(b) 1 h, (c) 5 h, (d) 9 h); the 1 h specimen still shows a dense tangled dislocation arrangement.

κ-carbides are mainly precipitated in the first hour of the 550 °C annealing treatment, while recovery (reduction of dislocation density) needs a longer time; longer annealing may coarsen κ-carbides, so the annealing time should be optimized to balance κ-carbide coarsening and dislocation-density reduction.
The measured (ICP) composition of the 3Cr strip is Mn 27.6, Al 8.4, C 1.3, Cr 2.8 wt.% (Fe balance), and its measured average density is 6.45 g/cm3.
